categories.label: Finish
categories.note: What has happened to the print since

items.t: Kept in a wallet for years. Soft corners, a crease down the middle, surface rubbed dull.
Rescued from a bin. One crumple, flattened out again, the crease network permanent.
Water damaged along one edge, colours run and feathered where the wet reached.
Sun bleached in a window. One half nearly gone, the other half fine.
Stuck up with tape four times. Tape marks and torn paper at each corner.
Printed at the wrong size and trimmed by hand, slightly crooked.
A test print with registration marks and colour bars still along one edge.
Second hand. A previous owner's name in biro in the corner.
Chewed. One corner has been in a mouth belonging to {4}.
Printed on the back of something else, the other side faintly showing through.
Screen printed by somebody learning. One colour laid on too heavy and still tacky.
Guillotine cut through part of the image, losing a few millimetres of one side.
A newspaper clipping, browned, with the edge of an unrelated advert attached.
Rolled up for a long time. It will not lie flat and the drawing curves with it.
Annotated by somebody in pencil. Small marks, no words.
Photographed rather than scanned, on a table, at a slight angle, with real shadow.
Held up by a hand at the edge of frame.
Pinned behind other pieces of paper, partially covered.
Immaculate and clearly never used, which is its own kind of sad.
Ink still wet in one area and smudged by a thumb pulling it off the press.
Static clinging to the surface, one hair stuck across it.
Reproduced badly in a cheap catalogue, colours shifted green.
Faded except where a frame protected the border, leaving a bright rectangle edge.
Repaired with tape on the reverse, the repair visible as a line through the front.
